# Results — Study 832 (High-Yield Credit Momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: the
**trend** (trailing 3-6-month total return) of **duration-hedged high-yield credit** —
HYG in excess of IEF — is a risk-on/off **timing** signal for equities (positive trend →
long SPY, negative → de-risk to IEF). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `3c027b47d765`
(the four-ETF close panel).*

Data as-of 2026-06-30. Fingerprint `3c027b47d765`.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **HYG, IEF, LQD, SPY**, 2007-05-01 → 2026-06-30, **4,822** dated rows |
| Cache | one parquet under this study's own `_cache/` (`fetch()` downloads once with up-to-4 retries; `load_panel()` reads it OFFLINE — no yfinance import) |
| Signal | **credit trend** = trailing-`L`-day total return of HYG **minus** IEF (duration-hedged), `L = 126` (6 months) as the headline, `L = 63` (3 months) as a cross-check; known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Timing rule | `risk_on = 1{trend > 0}` → hold **SPY** on day `t`; else hold **IEF**. Benchmark = 100%-SPY buy-and-hold |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: trend through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. A SPY↔IEF switch turns the book over (sell one, buy the other = **2 legs**), charged `cost_bps` one-way each × NAV on the switch day; long-only, no borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the risk-on−risk-off equity-excess difference (via a time-ordered regime-contrast series); a Welch *t*; a 1,000-draw label-shift placebo; a two-era cut; a Newey-West *t* on the timer's daily active return; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** HYG, IEF, LQD and SPY are all live,
continuously-listed ETFs, so the *tape* carries **no delisting bias**. The Signal-axis
caveat is different and just as real: this is **one** US credit history (2007-2026,
essentially a single realised path through the GFC, the 2015-16 HY wobble, COVID and the
2022 sell-off). A binary risk-on/off timer fit on one regime path is exposed to
single-sample overfit; the era split below is the honesty check.

## The signal — does the credit trend discriminate forward equity risk?

We split the day-`t` equity-excess-over-duration return `xs = r_SPY − r_IEF` by the credit
trend known at `t−1`. If a positive trend genuinely precedes SPY out-earning IEF, risk-on
days should show a **higher** `xs` than risk-off days (a positive difference).

| horizon | risk-on `xs` | risk-off `xs` | difference (on − off) | NW(10) *t* | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **126-day (6-month), n = 4,695** | +2.99 bps | +4.60 bps | **−1.62 bps/day** | **−0.37** | −0.32 |
| 63-day (3-month), n = 4,758 | +2.64 bps | +5.19 bps | **−2.55 bps/day** | **−0.61** | −0.51 |

The claimed edge **does not appear** — and what little there is points the **wrong way**.
At both the 3- and 6-month horizons the risk-on (positive-trend) days actually earned a
*lower* equity excess than the risk-off days (difference −1.6 / −2.5 bps/day), and the
Newey-West *t* is a negligible −0.37 / −0.61. Risk-on days are the *majority* (63.6% of the
sample), i.e. the timer is mostly long SPY anyway; conditioning on the credit trend adds no
discrimination.

## Placebo — is the (tiny, wrong-sign) difference even distinguishable from noise?

Keep the day-`t` equity-excess series but **circularly shift** the risk-on labels by a
random offset (breaks the trend→outcome link, preserves autocorrelation and the risk-on
share), 1,000 draws (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed difference | **−1.62 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.26 bps (4.67) |
| position of observed | ≈ **−0.4σ** (right-tail p = 0.646) |

The observed −1.62 bps sits **inside** the placebo cloud (−0.4σ, p = 0.65): the credit-trend
labelling carries no information the shuffled labels don't. There is nothing to explain.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2017-01-01)

| era | difference (on − off) | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2007-01 → 2017-01 (n=2,310) | **+4.80 bps** | +0.81 |
| 2017-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,385) | **−12.27 bps** | −1.81 |

The sign **flips across eras** (+4.80 bps early, −12.27 bps late) and neither half clears
|*t*| ≥ 1. This is the signature of a non-signal: an unstable, sample-dependent wobble, not
a persistent risk-on/off timer.

## The timer — can the switch beat buy-and-hold?

`risk_on` → SPY, else IEF, costed; compared to a 100%-SPY buy-and-hold. 201 switches over
19 years (≈11/yr).

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | net CAGR | B&H CAGR | net maxDD | B&H maxDD | active/day | active NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp/leg** | **0.627** | 0.619 | +7.32% | +10.87% | −41.3% | −54.7% | −1.76 bps | **−1.26** |
| **5 bps/leg** | 0.558 | 0.619 | +6.40% | +10.87% | −42.8% | −54.7% | −2.10 bps | −1.50 |

The timer's **only** real benefit is a shallower drawdown (−41% vs −55%): sitting in IEF
through risk-off stretches dodges some of the worst equity air-pockets. But it is **not an
edge**. On a risk-adjusted basis the net Sharpe at 1 bp (0.627) is a statistically
insignificant hair above buy-and-hold (0.619) — the daily active return is *negative*
(−1.76 bps/day, NW *t* = −1.26) — and by a realistic 5 bps/leg the net Sharpe (0.558) falls
**below** buy-and-hold. On raw return the timer forfeits **3.5%/yr of CAGR** (7.3% vs 10.9%)
by parking in bonds during the 2010s bull. It is drawdown *insurance you pay for in forgone
return*, not a timing premium.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent risk-on factor that drives the
duration-hedged credit trend and (with `edge > 0`) the *forward* SPY excess-over-IEF. No
network.

| world | discrimination NW *t* | timer vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.16** (sd 1.00), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | — |
| planted (`edge = 0.006`, seed 832) | **+2.99** (Welch *t* = +4.67) | active NW *t* = **+3.08**, timer Sharpe +0.52 vs B&H −1.01 |

The detector never fires on the null and cleanly recovers a *planted* credit-times-equity
relation — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine absence, not a broken engine. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The credit **trend** (HYG excess over IEF) does **not** time equity
  risk-on/off. At the claimed 3- and 6-month horizons the risk-on−risk-off equity-excess
  difference is **wrong-signed and negligible** (−1.62 bps/day, NW *t* = **−0.37** at 6
  months; −2.55 bps, *t* = −0.61 at 3 months), it sits **inside** a label-shift placebo
  (−0.4σ, p = 0.65), and it **flips sign across eras** (+4.80 → −12.27 bps, |*t*| < 2 in
  both). A clean 20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* effect, so the flat result
  is a true absence. The credit trend is a risk-on/off *description*, not a forward equity
  *forecast*.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The SPY↔IEF timer never robustly beats buy-and-hold: net Sharpe
  0.627 vs 0.619 at 1 bp/leg is an insignificant hair (active NW *t* = **−1.26**, active
  return *negative*), it forfeits **3.5%/yr of CAGR**, and by 5 bps/leg its Sharpe (0.558)
  falls below buy-and-hold. Its one honest merit — a −41% vs −55% max drawdown — is
  insurance bought with forgone return, not a paycheck.
